name: Falcon3 7B Instruct
notes: Falcon3 is NOT a Mamba or hybrid model - config.json declares architectures ['LlamaForCausalLM'], model_type 'llama'. It is a plain dense GQA transformer. What is unusual is the head geometry, and it is worth recording for GEMM efficiency: hidden_size 3072 is narrow for a 7B model, depth is only 28 layers, and head_dim is 256 with just 12 query heads and 4 KV heads (gqa_ratio 3). That inverts the usual 8B recipe of 4096 hidden / 32 layers / 32 heads: the projection GEMMs are narrower but fewer, and head_dim 256 (vs the 128 standard for this size class) means 12 heads instead of 32, so the attention block carries 4 * 3072 * 3072 = 37.7M params/layer against the MLP's 3 * 3072 * 23040 = 212.3M - a 5.6:1 MLP-to-attention ratio. With intermediate_size 23040 the MLP is 7.5x hidden_size, so essentially all of this model's FLOPs and weight bytes sit in the MLP, and the narrow hidden_size makes it a poor fit for tensor-core tiles that prefer 4096-wide matrices. rope_theta 1000042, no rope_scaling, 32768 native context, vocab 131072 (untied embeddings = 2 x 131072 x 3072 = 805M params, 11% of the model). KV bytes/token at bf16 (2 bytes/element): 28 layers x 4 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 (K and V) x 2 bytes = 114,688 B/token = 112.0 KiB/token. The 256-wide heads make each KV head twice as wide as a 128-head_dim model's, but comparing against Llama-3.1-8B (32 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 x 2 x 2 = 131,072 B/token) Falcon3 is 12.5% SMALLER overall, because 4 fewer layers and 4 fewer KV heads outweigh the doubled head width. Falcon3 gets a slightly cheaper KV cache than its nominal size class suggests.
